```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  message = TRUE,
  warning = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

Models the probability of recovering SBS88 from a simulated branch as a
function of background mutation burden and SBS88 proportion, then
reparameterises that model in terms of branch duration and colibactin
intensity.

Three figures are produced:

| File | Question |
|---|---|
| `01_detection_limit.png` | Minimum detectable SBS88, relative and absolute, against background burden |
| `02_min_intensity_by_duration.png` | Minimum colibactin intensity against branch duration |
| `03_minimum_sbs88_proportion_by_background_mutations.png` | As `01a`, overlaid with the observed paediatric branches |

## Setup

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(ggnewscale)
  library(mgcv)
  library(patchwork)
})

set.seed(42)
```

### Configuration

Set `dataset` to `"pruned"` or `"unpruned"`. Everything downstream — input
file, column handling and output directory — follows from this one switch, so
the two runs write to separate folders and cannot overwrite each other.

```{r config}
dataset <- "unpruned"          # <-- "pruned" or "unpruned"

stopifnot(dataset %in% c("pruned", "unpruned"))

# Background (SBS1+SBS5+SBS18) mutations per year in a single crypt lineage
background_rate <- 38

# Detection probabilities to report. 1 - sqrt(0.05) is the per-branch
# probability giving a 5% joint false-negative rate across two branches.
targets <- c(1 - sqrt(0.05), 0.9)
 
fn_levels <- c("1% False Negative", "5% False Negative", "25% False Negative")
fn5_target <- 1 - sqrt(0.05)       # 0.7764

fn_label <- function(target) {
  factor(sprintf("%.0f%% False Negative", 100 * (1 - target)^2), levels = fn_levels)
}
 

n_draws <- 2000   # posterior draws for confidence intervals
grid_n  <- 200    # grid resolution per axis

in_dir  <- "/Users/hm14/volumes/hm14_lustre/team267/users/hm14/paediatric_colon_project/mutational_signatures/msa_dir/MSA/output_tables/branches_rate_SBS88/"
crypt_pileup_dir <- "/Users/hm14/Documents/GitHub/ChildhoodColibactinExposure/Data/"
ground_truth_dir <- '/Users/hm14/volumes/hm14_lustre/team267/users/hm14/paediatric_colon_project/mutational_signatures/simulation_variation_sbs88/01_Input/'
out_dir <- file.path("/Users/hm14/Documents/modelling_colibactin_intensity/", paste0(dataset, "_attribution"))
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

message("Dataset: ", dataset, " -> ", out_dir)
```

### Input files

```{r input-paths}
sim_inputs <- list(
  pruned = list(
    file       = file.path(in_dir, "pruned_attribution_branches_rate_SBS88_SBS_abs_mutations.csv"),
    sample_col = "X",
    # Pruned table reports absolute mutation counts
    relative   = FALSE
  ),
  unpruned = list(
    file       = file.path(in_dir, "output_branches_rate_SBS88_SBS_weights_table.csv"),
    sample_col = "Sample",
    # Weights table reports fractions; rescale by the ground-truth total
    relative   = TRUE 
  )
)

cfg <- sim_inputs[[dataset]]
```

```{r load-data}
ground_truth <- read.table(
  file.path(ground_truth_dir, "ground_truth_exposures_branches_rate_SBS88.txt"),
  sep = "\t", header = TRUE
) %>%
  # Ground-truth file stores signature fractions; convert to mutation counts
  mutate(across(contains("SBS"), ~ .x * burdens))

attribution <- read.csv(cfg$file)
```




### Build the simulation dataframe

One function for both inputs, producing identical column names
(`*_called` vs `*_ground_truth`) whichever dataset is selected. The original
script named the unpruned background column `SBSbackground_pruned`, which was
a copy-paste artefact.

```{r prepare-sim-df}
prepare_sim_df <- function(attribution, ground_truth, sample_col, relative,
                           background_rate) {

  out <- attribution %>%
    dplyr::rename(sample = all_of(sample_col)) %>%
    left_join(ground_truth, by = "sample", suffix = c("_called", "_ground_truth"))

  if (relative) {
    out <- out %>%
      mutate(across(
        ends_with("_called"),
        ~ .x * (SBS1_ground_truth + SBS5_ground_truth +
                SBS18_ground_truth + SBS88_ground_truth)
      ))
  }

  out %>%
    mutate(
      SBSbackground_called       = SBS1_called + SBS5_called + SBS18_called,
      SBSbackground_ground_truth = SBS1_ground_truth + SBS5_ground_truth + SBS18_ground_truth,
      class = case_when(
        SBS88_called >  0 & SBS88_ground_truth >  0 ~ "TP",
        SBS88_called == 0 & SBS88_ground_truth >  0 ~ "FN",
        SBS88_called == 0 & SBS88_ground_truth == 0 ~ "TN",
        TRUE                                        ~ "FP"
      ),
      sample_age = SBSbackground_ground_truth / background_rate,
      # CHECK THIS. If SBS1+SBS5+SBS18+SBS88 already sums to `burdens` (which the
      # rescaling above implies), the fraction of the total is SBS88 / burdens,
      # not SBS88 / (burdens + SBS88). See the note in the README.
      SBS88_ground_truth_proportion = SBS88_ground_truth / (burdens + SBS88_ground_truth),
      SBS88_rate = SBS88_ground_truth / sample_age
    )
}

sim_df <- prepare_sim_df(
  attribution, ground_truth,
  sample_col      = cfg$sample_col,
  relative        = cfg$relative,
  background_rate = background_rate
)

dplyr::count(sim_df, class)
```

## Detection model

### Prepare the modelling frame

```{r model-frame}
dat <- sim_df %>%
  transmute(
    class  = as.character(class),
    burden = as.numeric(SBSbackground_ground_truth),
    prop   = as.numeric(SBS88_ground_truth_proportion)
  )

if (max(dat$prop, na.rm = TRUE) > 1.001) {
  stop("SBS88 proportion exceeds 1 - check the denominator in `prepare_sim_df`.")
}

negatives <- dat %>% filter(class %in% c("TN", "FP"))
fp_rate   <- mean(negatives$class == "FP")

pos <- dat %>%
  filter(class %in% c("TP", "FN"), burden > 0, prop > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    detected   = as.integer(class == "TP"),
    log_burden = log10(burden),
    log_prop   = log10(prop),
    # burden is background-only, so total = background / (1 - prop)
    n_sbs88    = burden * prop / (1 - prop)
  )

message(sprintf("Negatives: %d (FP rate %.4f) | Positives: %d (detected %d, missed %d)",
                nrow(negatives), fp_rate, nrow(pos),
                sum(pos$detected), sum(!pos$detected)))
```

### Fit and select

```{r fit-models}
# Tensor smooth; k kept modest because the transition is informed by a small
# number of missed samples.
m_gam <- gam(detected ~ te(log_burden, log_prop, k = c(5, 5)),
             family = binomial, data = pos, method = "REML")

# Parametric counterpart: closed-form, quotable, and a guard against the GAM
# chasing noise.
m_glm <- gam(detected ~ log_burden + log_prop,
             family = binomial, data = pos, method = "REML")

cat(sprintf("AIC: GAM %.1f, linear %.1f (lower is better)\n", AIC(m_gam), AIC(m_glm)))

# Use the simpler model unless the smooth earns its complexity
use_gam     <- AIC(m_gam) < AIC(m_glm) - 2
model       <- if (use_gam) m_gam else m_glm
model_label <- if (use_gam) "GAM (tensor smooth)" else "logistic, linear in log-log"
message("Using: ", model_label)

cf <- coef(m_glm)
message(sprintf("Linear model: logit(P) = %.3f + %.3f*log10(burden) + %.3f*log10(prop)",
                cf[1], cf[2], cf[3]))
message(sprintf("  => P=0.5 limit: prop = %.4g * burden^%.3f",
                10^(-cf[1] / cf[3]), -cf[2] / cf[3]))
```

### Calibration check

The figures below are meaningless if the model does not reproduce the data it
was fitted to. Bins are equal-count on the **linear predictor**: most samples
sit at P ~ 1, so probability quantiles collapse to duplicate cut points and
hide the transition.

```{r calibration}
wilson <- function(k, n, z = 1.96) {
  p <- k / n; d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  half <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  c((p + z^2 / (2 * n) - half) / d, (p + z^2 / (2 * n) + half) / d)
}

pos <- pos %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = ., type = "response")),
    eta    = as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = ., type = "link"))
  )

calib <- pos %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(eta, 12)) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), k = sum(detected),
            expected = mean(fitted), observed = mean(detected), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(lower = wilson(k, n)[1], upper = wilson(k, n)[2]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(outside = expected < lower | expected > upper)

print(as.data.frame(calib), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

cat(sprintf("\nOverall: %d missed, %.1f expected by the model\n",
            sum(!pos$detected), sum(1 - pos$fitted)))

high_conf   <- pos$fitted > 0.95
unexplained <- sum(high_conf & pos$detected == 0)
cat(sprintf("Misses at fitted P > 0.95: %d (model expects %.1f)\n",
            unexplained, sum(1 - pos$fitted[high_conf])))

if (unexplained > 3 * sum(1 - pos$fitted[high_conf])) {
  warning("Substantial detection failures in the high-confidence region. The ",
          "covariates do not explain all false negatives - consider a floor term ",
          "before quoting the limits.")
}
```

## Figure 01: detection limit against background burden

Posterior draws over a 2D grid, then the SBS88 level at which each target
detection probability is crossed.

```{r posterior-grid}
beta_hat   <- coef(model)
beta_draws <- mgcv::rmvn(n_draws, beta_hat, vcov(model))

burden_grid <- 10^seq(log10(min(pos$burden)), log10(max(pos$burden)), length.out = grid_n)
prop_grid   <- 10^seq(log10(min(pos$prop)),   log10(max(pos$prop)),   length.out = grid_n)

pred_grid <- expand.grid(log_burden = log10(burden_grid), log_prop = log10(prop_grid)) %>%
  mutate(burden = 10^log_burden, prop = 10^log_prop)

Xp      <- predict(model, newdata = pred_grid, type = "lpmatrix")
p_draws <- plogis(Xp %*% t(beta_draws))   # grid rows x draws
```

```{r detection-limits}
# Named `crossing_point` so it does not mask tidyr::crossing.
# cummax enforces monotonicity against numerical wobble.
crossing_point <- function(p, x_log, target) {
  if (all(p < target) || all(p > target)) return(NA_real_)
  approx(cummax(p), x_log, xout = target, ties = "ordered")$y
}

burden_index <- split(seq_len(nrow(pred_grid)), pred_grid$log_burden)

limits <- lapply(targets, function(tg) {
  out <- vapply(burden_index, function(idx) {
    idx <- idx[order(pred_grid$log_prop[idx])]
    vapply(seq_len(n_draws),
           function(d) crossing_point(p_draws[idx, d], pred_grid$log_prop[idx], tg),
           numeric(1))
  }, numeric(n_draws))
  data.frame(
    target = tg,
    burden = 10^as.numeric(names(burden_index)),
    fit    = 10^apply(out, 2, median,   na.rm = TRUE),
    lower  = 10^apply(out, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper  = 10^apply(out, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_na   = apply(out, 2, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  # Drop burdens where the target is unreachable in most draws
  filter(n_na < 0.1) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sbs88       = burden * fit   / (1 - fit),
    n_sbs88_lower = burden * lower / (1 - lower),
    n_sbs88_upper = burden * upper / (1 - upper),
    target_label  = sprintf("%d%% detection", round(target * 100))
  )

if (min(limits$n_sbs88, na.rm = TRUE) < 1) {
  warning("Fitted limit implies fewer than one SBS88 mutation - check the ",
          "proportion denominator.")
}
```

## Figure 01: detection limit against background burden
 
Posterior draws over a 2D grid, then the SBS88 level at which each target
detection probability is crossed.
 
### Numeric inversion
 
All three figures invert the same fitted surface: hold one quantity fixed,
sweep the other, find where P(detect) crosses a target. Doing this on a grid
rather than in closed form means it works for the GAM as well as the linear
model, so no figure depends on which one AIC selects.
 
```{r inversion-helpers}
beta_draws <- mgcv::rmvn(n_draws, coef(model), vcov(model))
 
# P(detect) per posterior draw: rows = newdata rows, cols = draws
p_draws_for <- function(newdata) {
  plogis(predict(model, newdata = newdata, type = "lpmatrix") %*% t(beta_draws))
}
 
# Named `crossing_point` so it does not mask tidyr::crossing.
# cummax enforces monotonicity against numerical wobble.
crossing_point <- function(p, x_log, target) {
  if (all(p < target) || all(p > target)) return(NA_real_)
  approx(cummax(p), x_log, xout = target, ties = "ordered")$y
}
 
# For each value in `fixed_grid`, sweep `solve_grid` and locate the crossing.
# `covariates(fixed, solve_grid)` builds the model's newdata.
invert_detection <- function(fixed_grid, solve_grid, covariates, target) {
  draws <- vapply(fixed_grid, function(v) {
    P <- p_draws_for(covariates(v, solve_grid))
    vapply(seq_len(n_draws),
           function(d) crossing_point(P[, d], log10(solve_grid), target),
           numeric(1))
  }, numeric(n_draws))
 
  data.frame(
    target = target,
    fixed  = fixed_grid,
    fit    = 10^apply(draws, 2, median,   na.rm = TRUE),
    lower  = 10^apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper  = 10^apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_na   = apply(draws, 2, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
  )
}
 
# --- Covariate maps -----------------------------------------------------------
# For a branch of duration dt, background accruing at r per year and SBS88 at
# intensity lambda:  burden = r * dt,  prop = lambda / (r + lambda).
 
cov_prop <- function(burden, prop_grid) {              # solve for proportion
  data.frame(log_burden = log10(burden), log_prop = log10(prop_grid))
}
 
cov_burden <- function(prop, burden_grid) {            # solve for burden
  data.frame(log_burden = log10(burden_grid), log_prop = log10(prop))
}
 
cov_intensity <- function(duration, intensity_grid) {  # solve for intensity
  data.frame(
    log_burden = log10(background_rate * duration),
    log_prop   = log10(intensity_grid / (background_rate + intensity_grid))
  )
}
 
cov_duration <- function(intensity, duration_grid) {   # solve for duration
  data.frame(
    log_burden = log10(background_rate * duration_grid),
    log_prop   = log10(intensity / (background_rate + intensity))
  )
}
 
# Anything outside these ranges is extrapolation. A tensor smooth extrapolates
# far less gracefully than a linear model, so this matters more when use_gam.
fit_burden_range <- range(pos$burden)
fit_prop_range   <- range(pos$prop)
 
warn_if_outside <- function(x, rng, what) {
  if (min(x) < rng[1] || max(x) > rng[2]) {
    warning(sprintf("%s grid spans %.3g-%.3g; model fitted over %.3g-%.3g.%s",
                    what, min(x), max(x), rng[1], rng[2],
                    if (use_gam) " The GAM extrapolates unreliably." else ""))
  }
}
```
 
```{r detection-limits}
burden_grid <- 10^seq(log10(fit_burden_range[1]), log10(fit_burden_range[2]),
                      length.out = grid_n)
prop_grid   <- 10^seq(log10(fit_prop_range[1]), log10(fit_prop_range[2]),
                      length.out = grid_n)
 
limits <- lapply(targets, function(tg)
  invert_detection(burden_grid, prop_grid, cov_prop, tg)) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::rename(burden = fixed) %>%
  # Drop burdens where the target is unreachable in most draws
  filter(n_na < 0.1) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sbs88         = burden * fit   / (1 - fit),
    n_sbs88_lower   = burden * lower / (1 - lower),
    n_sbs88_upper   = burden * upper / (1 - upper),
    fn_target_label = fn_label(target)
  )
 
if (min(limits$n_sbs88, na.rm = TRUE) < 1) {
  warning("Fitted limit implies fewer than one SBS88 mutation - check the ",
          "proportion denominator.")
}
```

 
Scaling of the absolute limit: if detection is Poisson-noise limited, the
number of SBS88 mutations needed grows as `sqrt(burden)`, i.e. an exponent of
0.5.
 
```{r limits-coverage}
# How much of each target's curve survived the `n_na` filter? A target whose
# crossing falls outside the prop grid at every burden is dropped entirely.
limits %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  summarise(
    n_burdens = n(),
    unusable  = sum(!is.finite(log10(n_sbs88))),
    fit_min   = min(fit), fit_max = max(fit),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
dropped <- setdiff(targets, unique(limits$target))
if (length(dropped)) {
  warning("No reachable limits for target(s): ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "),
          ". Widen `prop_grid` or relax the `n_na` threshold.")
}
```
 
```{r scaling-absolute}
# Iterate over the targets actually present, not the requested ones, and keep
# only rows where log10() is defined. `fit` >= 1 makes burden*fit/(1-fit)
# negative, and log10 of that is NaN.
fit_scaling <- function(sub, tg) {
  sub <- sub %>% filter(is.finite(log10(n_sbs88)), is.finite(log10(burden)))
 
  if (nrow(sub) < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("  %2d%% detection: skipped, only %d usable burden(s)\n",
                round(tg * 100), nrow(sub)))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
 
  f  <- lm(log10(n_sbs88) ~ log10(burden), data = sub)
  ci <- confint(f)[2, ]
  cat(sprintf("  %2d%% detection: k = %.3f (%.3f-%.3f), n = %d%s\n",
              round(tg * 100), coef(f)[2], ci[1], ci[2], nrow(sub),
              if (ci[1] <= 0.5 && ci[2] >= 0.5) "  [consistent with sqrt(burden)]" else ""))
}
 
for (tg in sort(unique(limits$target))) {
  fit_scaling(limits %>% filter(target == tg), tg)
}
```
 
## Observed paediatric branches
 
Loaded before the remaining figures, which overlay these points. In the
original script `df_clean` was created in the last chunk but used two chunks
earlier, so a clean top-to-bottom run failed.
 
```{r load-observed}
crypt_pileup_sig_annotated <- read.csv(file.path(crypt_pileup_dir, "crypt_pileup_classification.csv"))

observed_branches <- crypt_pileup_sig_annotated %>%
  filter(SBS88_branch > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    age_branch_start = background_muts_branch_start_msa / background_muts_rate_msa,
    age_branch_end   = background_muts_branch_end_msa   / background_muts_rate_msa,
    branch_duration  = age_branch_end - age_branch_start,
    SBS88_intensity  = SBS88_branch / branch_duration,
    SBS88_proportion = SBS88_branch / (SBS88_branch + background_muts_branch)
  ) %>%
  # Some branches have SBS1+SBS5 = 0 because of high SBS88 attribution
  filter(branch_duration > 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(patient, crypt, age, SBS88_branch, SBS88_intensity,
                branch_duration, background_muts_branch, age_branch_end,
                SBS88_proportion)
 
range(observed_branches$SBS88_proportion)
```
 
## Figure 02: minimum intensity by branch duration
 
Both axes are reparameterisations of the burden/proportion surface, so the
grids are bounded by the fitted burden range rather than chosen freely.
 
```{r fig-07-data}
lambda <- as.numeric(quantile(observed_branches$SBS88_intensity, 0.05))
 
duration_grid  <- 10^seq(log10(fit_burden_range[1] / background_rate),
                         log10(fit_burden_range[2] / background_rate),
                         length.out = grid_n)
intensity_grid <- background_rate * prop_grid / (1 - prop_grid)
 
warn_if_outside(background_rate * duration_grid, fit_burden_range, "Duration")
 
# Minimum branch duration at the observed 5th-percentile intensity
q_duration <- invert_detection(lambda, duration_grid, cov_duration, fn5_target)
 
cat(sprintf("%.1f years (95%% CI %.1f-%.1f), i.e. %.0f background mutations\n",
            q_duration$fit, q_duration$lower, q_duration$upper,
            q_duration$fit * background_rate))
 
min_intensity <- lapply(targets, function(tg)
  invert_detection(duration_grid, intensity_grid, cov_intensity, tg)) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  filter(n_na < 0.1) %>%
  dplyr::rename(duration = fixed) %>%
  mutate(fn_target_label = fn_label(target))
 
# Consistency: the inverse round-trips (to grid tolerance, in log space), and a
# stricter target always demands more intensity.
if (!is.na(q_duration$fit)) {
  rt <- invert_detection(q_duration$fit, intensity_grid, cov_intensity, fn5_target)
  stopifnot(abs(log10(rt$fit) - log10(lambda)) < 0.05)
}
 
chk <- min_intensity %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = duration, names_from = target, values_from = fit) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()
stopifnot(all(diff(t(chk[, -1])) >= 0))
```
 
```{r fig-07, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5}
p2 <- ggplot(min_intensity,
                 aes(duration, fit, colour = fn_target_label, fill = fn_target_label)) +
  geom_point(data = observed_branches,
             aes(branch_duration, SBS88_intensity), size=3,inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = lambda, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q_duration$fit, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  
  geom_text( data = data.frame(x = 0.1, y = 0.1, size=5,label = paste0("Estimated minimum branch duration: ", round(q_duration$fit, 1), " years")),
  aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),inherit.aes = FALSE,size=5,hjust = 0,vjust = 0)+
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(0.1, 17)) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 2000)) +
  labs(x = "Branch duration (years)",
       y = "Minimum detectable SBS88 intensity\n(mutations/year)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = paste0('MSA attribution - ',dataset),
       subtitle = "Points: observed branches from paediatric crypts | Dashed: 5th percentile intensity")+
  theme_classic()+
   theme(legend.position='none',
        title=element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        axis.text=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text=element_text(size=14))
```
 
Scaling: Poisson-limited detection implies `lambda_min ~ dt^-0.5`.
 
```{r scaling-intensity}
for (tg in sort(unique(min_intensity$target))) {
  sub <- min_intensity %>%
    filter(target == tg, is.finite(log10(fit)), is.finite(log10(duration)))
 
  if (nrow(sub) < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("  %2d%%: skipped, only %d usable duration(s)\n",
                round(tg * 100), nrow(sub)))
    next
  }
 
  f  <- lm(log10(fit) ~ log10(duration), data = sub)
  ci <- confint(f)[2, ]
  cat(sprintf("  %2d%%: k = %.3f (%.3f to %.3f), n = %d%s\n",
              round(tg * 100), coef(f)[2], ci[1], ci[2], nrow(sub),
              if (ci[1] <= -0.5 && ci[2] >= -0.5) "  [consistent with dt^-0.5]" else ""))
}
```
 
## Figure 03: minimum proportion by background burden
 
This solves the same quantity as figure 03, over the burden range spanned by
the observed branches, with those branches overlaid.
 
```{r fig-09-data}
prop <- as.numeric(quantile(observed_branches$SBS88_proportion, 0.05))
stopifnot(prop > 0, prop < 1)
 
# The original swept 10^0 to 10^4, far outside the fitted range. Clamp to the
# union of the fitted range and the observed branches, and warn on the overhang.
burden_grid_09 <- 10^seq(
  log10(min(fit_burden_range[1], min(observed_branches$background_muts_branch))),
  log10(max(fit_burden_range[2], max(observed_branches$background_muts_branch))),
  length.out = grid_n
)
warn_if_outside(burden_grid_09, fit_burden_range, "Figure 09 burden")
 
q_burden <- invert_detection(prop, burden_grid_09, cov_burden, fn5_target)
 
cat(sprintf("%.0f background mutations (95%% CI %.0f-%.0f); %.0f total, %.1f SBS88\n",
            q_burden$fit, q_burden$lower, q_burden$upper,
            q_burden$fit / (1 - prop), q_burden$fit * prop / (1 - prop)))
 
prop_limits <- lapply(targets, function(tg)
  invert_detection(burden_grid_09, prop_grid, cov_prop, tg)) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  filter(n_na < 0.1, fit <= 1) %>%     # a proportion above 1 is unreachable
  dplyr::rename(burden = fixed) %>%
  mutate(fn_target_label = fn_label(target))
 
if (!is.na(q_burden$fit)) {
  rt <- invert_detection(q_burden$fit, prop_grid, cov_prop, fn5_target)
  stopifnot(abs(log10(rt$fit) - log10(prop)) < 0.05)
}
```
 
```{r fig-09, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5}
p3 <- ggplot(prop_limits,
                 aes(burden, fit, colour = fn_target_label, fill = fn_target_label)) +
  geom_point(data = observed_branches,
             aes(background_muts_branch, SBS88_proportion),size=3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = prop, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q_burden$fit, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text( data = data.frame(x = 0.1, y = 0.01, size=5,label = paste0("Estimated minimum length: ", round(q_burden$fit, 0), " mutations")),
  aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),inherit.aes = FALSE,size=5,hjust = 0,vjust = 0)+
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = "Background mutation burden", y = "Minimum detectable SBS88 proportion",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = paste0("MSA attribution - ",dataset))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position='none',
        title=element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        axis.text=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text=element_text(size=14))

```
